title: All About Grasshoppers
checkpoint: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — non-fiction, real facts about grasshoppers.
note_for_grown_ups: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — non-fiction, real facts about grasshoppers.

pages.text: Nell spots a green bug in the long grass.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee hovering just above a bright green grasshopper perched on a blade of long grass.

pages.text: A bug like this has long back legs.
pages.illustration: A close-up of the grasshopper, its long, bent back legs clearly visible.

pages.text: A bug like this can jump a long way.
pages.illustration: The grasshopper mid-jump, leaping a great distance across the grass.

pages.text: A bug like this has a pair of long feelers.
pages.illustration: A close-up of the grasshopper’s head, showing two long thin feelers.

pages.text: A bug like this can sing. It taps its back legs to make the sound.
pages.illustration: The grasshopper rubbing its back legs together, a sound coming from the motion.

pages.text: Nell stops to hear the song.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee pausing in the air, listening intently to the grasshopper’s song.

pages.text: A bug like this is green to hide in the grass.
pages.illustration: The grasshopper blending in almost perfectly with the green blades of grass around it.

pages.text: Nell can hardly spot it when it sits still.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee looking closely, the grasshopper nearly invisible against the grass.

pages.text: The bug jumps off into the long grass.
pages.illustration: The grasshopper leaping away in a big jump, disappearing into the tall grass.
Nell the bee smiling, watching the spot where the grasshopper vanished into the grass.
